questions.knowledgeNote: Draw the circumdiameter through C: angle CBD is 90 deg, so sinA = a/(2R).
questions.question: AQ1(i). State and establish the sine law. (T.U. 2055S)
questions.solution: Statement: in any triangle ABC, a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC = 2R where R is the circumradius. Proof: let O be the circumcentre and extend CO to meet the circumcircle at D, so CD = 2R is a diameter and angle CBD = 90 deg (angle in a semicircle). Angles CAD... angle CDB equals angle CAB = A (angles in the same segment subtend CB). In right triangle CBD, sin(angle CDB) = BC/CD = a/(2R), so sinA = a/(2R), i.e. a/sinA = 2R. The same construction at the other vertices gives b/sinB = c/sinC = 2R.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q1(i) (T.U. 2055S); book p188 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Projection is sine law + sin(B+C) expansion; tangent law is (sinB - sinC)/(sinB + sinC) plus sum-to-product.
questions.question: AQ1(ii). State the sine law. Use this law to prove the projection law a = b*cosC + c*cosB and the tangent law tan((B-C)/2) = [(b-c)/(b+c)]*cot(A/2) (with cyclic form tan((A-B)/2) = [(a-b)/(a+b)]*cot(C/2)). (T.U. 2057S) (HSEB 2050; cyclic form HSEB 2058)
questions.solution: Sine law: a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC = 2R. Projection: b*cosC + c*cosB = 2R*sinB*cosC + 2R*sinC*cosB = 2R*sin(B+C) = 2R*sinA = a. Tangent law: (b-c)/(b+c) = (sinB - sinC)/(sinB + sinC) = [2*cos((B+C)/2)*sin((B-C)/2)]/[2*sin((B+C)/2)*cos((B-C)/2)] = tan((B-C)/2)*cot((B+C)/2) = tan((B-C)/2)*tan(A/2) (since (B+C)/2 = (pi-A)/2). Hence tan((B-C)/2) = [(b-c)/(b+c)]*cot(A/2). The cyclic form tan((A-B)/2) = [(a-b)/(a+b)]*cot(C/2) (top of book p189, tags T.U. 2057S, HSEB 2058) follows by the same steps with permuted letters.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q1(ii) (T.U. 2057S) (HSEB 2050); book p188 = PDF p216, cyclic form top of book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC is the sine law restated as a continued proportion.
questions.question: AQ2. In any triangle ABC, prove that a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC. (HSEB 2058)
questions.solution: By the sine law each of a/sinA, b/sinB, c/sinC equals 2R, so all three are equal.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q2 (HSEB 2058); book pp188-189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: The common value 2R is the circumdiameter: each side is a chord subtending its angle at the centre.
questions.question: AQ3. In any triangle, prove that a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC = 2R, where R is the radius of the circumcircle. (HSEB 2051, 2052, 2055)
questions.solution: From AQ1(i), a/sinA = 2R where 2R is the diameter of the circumcircle through the construction with diameter CD = 2R. Repeating at each vertex, b/sinB = c/sinC = 2R as well, so all four expressions are equal.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q3 (HSEB 2051, 1952... i.e. 2051, 2052, 2055); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cos(C/2) = sqrt[s(s-c)/(ab)]; the B-forms follow by cyclic permutation: sin(B/2) = sqrt[(s-a)(s-c)/(ac)], tan(B/2) = sqrt[(s-a)(s-c)/(s(s-b))].
questions.question: AQ4. In any triangle ABC, prove that cos(C/2) = sqrt[s(s-c)/(ab)], and write the similar results for sin(B/2) and tan(B/2). (HSEB 2054)
questions.solution: cos^2(C/2) = (1+cosC)/2 = [1 + (a^2+b^2-c^2)/(2ab)]/2 = [(a+b)^2 - c^2]/(4ab) = [(a+b-c)(a+b+c)]/(4ab) = [2(s-c)*2s]/(4ab) = s(s-c)/(ab). Since C/2 is acute, cos(C/2) = sqrt[s(s-c)/(ab)]. Similarly sin(B/2) = sqrt[(s-a)(s-c)/(ac)] (from sin^2(B/2) = (1-cosB)/2) and tan(B/2) = sin(B/2)/cos(B/2) = sqrt[(s-a)(s-c)/(s(s-b))].
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q4 (HSEB 2054); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.question: AQ5. Prove that cos(A/2) = sqrt[s(s-a)/(bc)]. (T.U. 2056S) (HSEB 2057)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q5 (T.U. 2056S) (HSEB 2057); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: c - a*cosB = 2R*sinC*cosB: expand sinC = sin(A+B) and watch sinB*cosB cancel.
questions.question: AQ6(i). In any triangle ABC, prove that (c - a*cosB)/(b - a*cosC) = sinB/sinC.
questions.solution: c - a*cosB = 2R*sinC - 2R*sinA*cosB = 2R*[sin(A+B) - sinA*cosB] = 2R*cosA*sinB. Likewise b - a*cosC = 2R*sinB - 2R*sinA*cosC = 2R*[sin(A+C) - sinA*cosC] = 2R*cosA*sinC. Dividing gives sinB/sinC.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q6(i); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cos^2B - cos^2C = sin^2C - sin^2B = (c-b)(c+b)/(4R^2): each fraction leaves (c-b)/(4R^2).
questions.question: AQ6(ii). Prove that [(cos^2B - cos^2C)/(b+c)] + [(cos^2C - cos^2A)/(c+a)] + [(cos^2A - cos^2B)/(a+b)] = 0.
questions.solution: cos^2B - cos^2C = (1 - sin^2B) - (1 - sin^2C) = sin^2C - sin^2B = (c^2-b^2)/(4R^2). Dividing by (b+c) gives (c-b)/(4R^2). Cyclically the second term is (a-c)/(4R^2) and the third is (b-a)/(4R^2). Adding: [(c-b) + (a-c) + (b-a)]/(4R^2) = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q6(ii); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sinB + sinC = 2*cos(A/2)*cos((B-C)/2) cancels the cosine, leaving 16R^2*sin^2(A/2)*cos(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2); the sum telescopes via (cosC - cosB)/2.
questions.question: AQ6(iii). Prove that [a^2*sin(B-C)/(sinB + sinC)] + [b^2*sin(C-A)/(sinC + sinA)] + [c^2*sin(A-B)/(sinA + sinB)] = 0.
questions.solution: a^2*sin(B-C) = 4R^2*sin^2A*2*sin((B-C)/2)*cos((B-C)/2) and sinB + sinC = 2*cos(A/2)*cos((B-C)/2), so the first term is 16R^2*sin^2(A/2)*cos(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2). Since cos(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2) = [cosC - cosB]/2 (from Q5(d) working), the first term equals 8R^2*sin^2(A/2)*(cosC - cosB). Cyclically summing: 8R^2*[sin^2(A/2)*(cosC - cosB) + sin^2(B/2)*(cosA - cosC) + sin^2(C/2)*(cosB - cosA)]. With sin^2(A/2) = (1-cosA)/2 this is 4R^2*[(1-cosA)(cosC - cosB) + (1-cosB)(cosA - cosC) + (1-cosC)(cosB - cosA)] = 4R^2*[(cosC - cosB + cosA - cosC + cosB - cosA) - (cosA*cosC - cosA*cosB + cosB*cosA - cosB*cosC + cosC*cosB - cosC*cosA)] = 4R^2*[0 - 0] = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q6(iii); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan(A/2)*tan(B/2) = r/(s-c)... no: use Delta: tan(A/2)*tan(B/2) = Delta^2/[(s(s-a))(s(s-b))]... simplest is (s-c)/s via r^2 = (s-a)(s-b)(s-c)/s.
questions.question: AQ6(iv). Prove that tan(A/2)*tan(B/2) = (a+b-c)/(a+b+c).
questions.solution: tan(A/2)*tan(B/2) = sqrt[(s-b)(s-c)/(s(s-a))] * sqrt[(s-a)(s-c)/(s(s-b))] = (s-c)/s. And (a+b-c)/(a+b+c) = 2(s-c)/(2s) = (s-c)/s. Both sides agree.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q6(iv); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.question: AQ6(v). Prove that (b-c)*cot(A/2) + (c-a)*cot(B/2) + (a-b)*cot(C/2) = 0.
questions.solution: (b-c)*cot(A/2) = 2R*(sinB - sinC)*cos(A/2)/sin(A/2) = 2R*2*cos((B+C)/2)*sin((B-C)/2)*cos(A/2)/sin(A/2) = 4R*sin((B-C)/2)*cos(A/2) = 2R*[cosC - cosB] (using 2*sin((B-C)/2)*cos(A/2) = cosC - cosB from Q5(d) working). Cyclically the others are 2R*(cosA - cosC) and 2R*(cosB - cosA). Adding: 2R*[(cosC - cosB) + (cosA - cosC) + (cosB - cosA)] = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q6(v); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Expand with cos^2(C/2) = (s(s-c))/(ab) style halves, or collect: LHS - c^2 = (a-b)^2 - 4ab*sin^2(C/2) - ... = 0 by the cosine rule.
questions.question: AQ6(vi). Prove that (a-b)^2*cos^2(C/2) + (a+b)^2*sin^2(C/2) = c^2.
questions.solution: With cos^2(C/2) = (1+cosC)/2 and sin^2(C/2) = (1-cosC)/2, the left side is [(a-b)^2*(1+cosC) + (a+b)^2*(1-cosC)]/2 = [(a-b)^2 + (a+b)^2]/2 + cosC*[(a-b)^2 - (a+b)^2]/2 = (2a^2+2b^2)/2 + cosC*(-4ab)/2 = (a^2+b^2) - 2ab*cosC = c^2 by the cosine rule.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Additional Questions (I) Q6(vi); book p189 = PDF p216 (vision read)
